The city council approved a new five-year transport plan yesterday. It includes two new tram lines, forty additional kilometres of bike lanes and a gradual reduction of car traffic in the historic centre. Some residents worry about higher parking fees and disruption during construction. Officials argue that the investments will shorten commutes and improve air quality. The first works are expected to start next spring, and public consultations will run until the end of the month.

Sleep is one of the most important restorative processes in the body. During sleep the brain organises information gathered during the day, strengthens memory traces and clears metabolic waste. Adults usually need seven to nine hours of sleep, yet many people sleep much less. Chronic sleep deprivation is linked to poorer concentration, higher risk of heart disease and weaker immunity. Experts recommend consistent bedtimes, fewer screens in the evening and a cool bedroom.
